paragraphs.text: The strangers: 1- The Jewish converts to Christianity who dwell in the countries of the world and are strangers far from Judea.
2- Believers in general are strangers in the world, because their homeland is heaven.
The dispersion: the Jewish converts to Christianity who were scattered because of the Jewish persecution of them in Judea and went to the various countries of the world.
Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia: countries located in Asia Minor, which is present-day Turkey.

The Apostle Peter addresses his epistle to the Jewish converts to Christianity who were scattered in the countries of Asia Minor, and also to all believers in the world who suffer persecutions because of their Christianity.
The foreknowledge of God: God the Father knows who will believe in Him, and this shows His love and care for His children from eternity.
Sanctification of the Spirit unto obedience: the Holy Spirit sanctifies believers and consecrates their hearts to obey God's commandments.

The sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: the blood of Christ, which saves those who believe in Him from their sins and gives them the heavenly Kingdom. He used the expression "sprinkling of blood," an expression from the Jewish Law, which sprinkled the blood of animals that were a type of the blood of Christ the Redeemer.
He sends the love of the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, who works in believers and grants them His grace and peace, which the Apostle Peter wishes for them and sends to them.
Offer words of encouragement, wishing God's work for those you meet, so that their hearts may rejoice and you may draw them to think about God and to rely on Him.

(2) The joys of salvation (vv. 3-8) 3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, 4 To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you, 5 Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. 6 Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations: 7 That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ: 8 Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:

Blessed be God the Father, who by His rich mercy gave us the new birth through Baptism. For man used to be born according to the flesh, under the rule of death, but he who is born according to the Spirit is a son of God and an heir with Christ, with a living hope in eternity, whose pledge is the resurrection of the Lord from the dead.
The characteristics of this spiritual inheritance are:
(1) Incorruptible: that is, remaining forever.
(2) Undefiled: it is not defiled by the sins that we left behind through repentance during our life on earth. (3) That fadeth not away: that is, it does not pass away.
(4) Reserved in heaven: God guards it for us and awaits us in heaven after we complete our striving on earth.
Let us hold fast to faith and hope with joy, and not despair because of present, temporary sufferings.
God keeps us in the faith and guards us from the wars of the devil, so that we may complete our striving and attain salvation on the great Day of Judgment.

This salvation gladdens your hearts, even though you will face trials and persecutions from the world that will grieve you for a time during your life on earth. But they do not take away your joy and peace, which will be completed in heaven, where all sorrows pass away.

He likens faith to gold that is refined by fire, so that its impurities are removed and its brightness appears. In the same way faith is purified of the impurities of weakness and sin through trials, which fire signifies, and so it becomes great (it is remembered), and God praises it on the Day of Judgment and because of it brings us into the glories of heaven.

During our life on earth we believe in Christ and love Him, so we endure afflictions for His sake, and our hearts rejoice in fellowship with Him, since we believe in His presence with us. Although we do not see Him with our physical eyes, we feel His work in us, and so we rejoice with a joy that cannot be expressed here on earth, as a pledge of the joys of heaven that we shall receive.

entries.section: (3) Salvation, the goal of the prophets

paragraphs.text: The Apostle directs believers to the fact that their goal in believing in Christ is to receive eternal salvation in the Kingdom of Heaven. We continue to receive this salvation on earth, as he says "receiving," and this takes place in the Church through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace. The original translation is "the salvation of your souls," not "the salvation of souls."

entries.section: (3) Salvation, the goal of the prophets

paragraphs.text: The salvation that Christ accomplished on the cross, and that we receive through the sacraments of the Church, was longed for and sought by the prophets, who prophesied about it in the Old Testament.

entries.section: (3) Salvation, the goal of the prophets

paragraphs.text: The Spirit of Christ which was in them: the Holy Spirit.

The Holy Spirit revealed to the prophets the life of Christ, His sufferings and His resurrection, but they did not know exactly the time of the fulfillment of this salvation. Even the prophet Daniel, to whom the time was revealed, did not grasp and understand these meanings because of the greatness of this salvation. There are many prophecies about the sufferings of Christ, such as (Isa 53, Dan 9:27), and likewise many prophecies about the resurrection of Christ and His ascension, such as (Ps 16:8-11, Isa 38:11).

entries.section: (3) Salvation, the goal of the prophets

paragraphs.text: The prophets understood that their prophecy would be fulfilled after a time and that they would not behold this salvation with their own eyes, but we, who have enjoyed this good news through the Apostles, have received this salvation. The angels also desired to see the fulfillment of this salvation of which they had heard. Thus the prophets were servants of salvation by their prophecies about it, and we received it in the New Testament through the redemption of Christ.

May your salvation from sin and your enjoyment of fellowship with Christ be your only goal, so that you are not hindered from it while you carry out your other aims. Rather, give up everything that hinders you, and remind yourself of this at the beginning of every day.
Wherefore: because of the importance of this salvation and its glories.
Gird up the loins of your mind: keep your thoughts under control, away from all evil, and be strengthened by the word of Christ for striving and pressing on in the way of the Kingdom.

Be sober: attentiveness and spiritual vigilance to reject all evil and to seize opportunities for life with God. The grace that is to be brought unto you: the complete salvation that you receive in the Kingdom.
At the revelation of Jesus Christ: the Day of Judgment, on which the righteous will be rewarded.
The Apostle defines our duties toward this salvation as follows:
First: readiness of mind. We must prepare our thoughts and be attentive, with all our senses and abilities, to spiritual striving.

Second: hope. We are not troubled by the sufferings of this temporary life, but rely with firm hope on the grace of God, which will grant us salvation in the Kingdom and compensate us for the toils of this life.

Third: repentance. Because believers are children of God, they must obey His commandments and repent of their former evil desires, in which they lived when they did not know Him and were far from Him before faith.
Fourth: holiness. He calls them to sanctify and consecrate their hearts to God by their good conduct, following the example of the holy Christ, as it is written in (Lev 11:44).
Fifth: walking in the fear of God:

If God is our tender Father, who redeemed us by His love on the cross, He is also the just Judge who judges our faults. Our attention to God's justice makes us fear Him and feel our estrangement from this perishing world, so we leave our sins, respect His presence with us and please Him in everything.

The fear of God protects you from every sin. So remember every day that you will meet God the just Judge, so that you repent, keep away from every evil that defiles you, live in holiness, and be at ease in every step you take.
Your vain conversation: your former life, which was far from God. Although it seemed upright, it did not truly qualify them to await Christ.
Received by tradition from your fathers: you learned it and acquired it from your Jewish fathers.
As of a lamb without blemish: in the Jewish Law, a lamb with no blemishes was offered as a sacrifice, and this was a type of Christ, who is slain for us on the cross.

He shows the greatness of the salvation that they receive in the Church, by which they were set free from slavery to sin and from the old life far from God. This was not by paying a material price such as silver and gold, which are perishing material things, but by paying the costliest price, which is the precious blood of Christ, which the blood of the animals offered in the Old Testament signified, and which is more precious and greater than the blood of animals.

This salvation was in God's eternal knowledge before He created the world. By His knowledge He knew that man would sin and need redemption, and by His love He was ready for that. The ordinances of the Old Testament were types and pointers to this salvation, which was manifested in the fullness of time by the blood of Christ, who saves everyone in the whole world who believes in Him.
By Him ye believe in God: through Christ the Redeemer your faith in God is strengthened and established.

The redemption of Christ, which fulfilled all the prophecies, establishes the faith of the Jews, especially after they learned that He rose from the dead and ascended in glory into heaven, so that their hope is fastened on eternity.

Since we have this salvation, we are careful to obey the commandments of Christ, which are the truth, and this with the help of the Holy Spirit. Then our hearts are purified from every sin, and we are able to love one another deeply and fervently from the heart.

The believer remembers that he has been born again of Christ the Word through the sacrament of Baptism, and not merely by the first, physical birth, which does not remove sin from man and exposes him to eternal torment, whereas the second birth prepares him to receive complete salvation in blessed eternity. He likens the physical birth to a seed that will die, that is, the body will decay in the dust, whereas the second birth is a spiritual seed, that is, it prepares us for the Kingdom of Heaven.

He likens the life of man on earth to grass, that is, a plant that lasts a few months and then falls and dries up. So also the life of man, with all its material glories, will end in death, however great the glory may seem, like beautiful flowers: it will wither, fall to the ground and die.
The good news which they received is the good news of Christ the Word, who gives us a life that endures forever in heaven.

Look at the grace of your knowing Christ and all that you receive from Him in the Church, so that you take care with your prayers in it and repent of your sins, and enjoy the blessings of salvation all the days of your life on earth until it is completed in heaven.
Christ the cornerstone and the characteristics of His children
Through Baptism we become children of God, and in our new life we must rid ourselves through repentance of all sins, among them:
Malice: insincerity.
Guile: deceit.
Hypocrisies: showing something other than what is inside.
Envy: wishing failure on others.
Evil speakings: anger together with abuse.
The sincere milk of the word: spiritual food, which includes Holy Communion, the word of God and all spiritual practices.

He likens believers who are born again of Baptism to infants who desire to drink pure, unadulterated milk from their mother the Church, that is, they should take care to be nourished by the Holy Sacraments, the Holy Bible, sermons, prayer and all spiritual things, so that they may continue in their spiritual growth.
If so be: since you have. "If" here expresses certainty, not doubt.

Because you have tasted the milk of the Church, the Mother, and have experienced the sweetness of fellowship with the good and tender Lord, to whom you draw near through prayers, worship and partaking of the Holy Sacraments, you will behold Him as a living stone on which your whole life rests. The likening of Christ to a stone is to affirm that He is the foundation of the spiritual building of every believer in Him, and He is a living stone because He is the living God and the giver of life to those who believe in Him.

The chief priests of the Jews rejected Christ and killed Him, relying on the greatness of their temple and their worship, all of which signify Him. But Christ is the only Son, chosen by God for the redemption of mankind, and He is the most precious and greatest of men; He is the example of the perfect man whom we ought to follow.

The Holy Bible has symbolized Christ by the stone in the rock that gave water in the wilderness to the children of Israel (Ex 17:6), by the stone cut out without hands as the prophet Daniel said (Dan 2:45), and by the stone of help that Samuel set up (1 Sam 7:12).

Do not be troubled if people reject your words and accuse you of what is not in you, so long as you hold fast to God's commandments. Seek His help, stand firm in your faith with meekness and gentleness, and be confident that God will in the end reveal your righteousness.
If Christ has been likened to the living stone to whom we come by faith and holy worship, the Apostle asks them to be:
Lively stones: that is, steadfast and firmly rooted in faith in Him, so that we live by His life.

A spiritual house: we all become members of one body, which is the Church, and it includes the saints in heaven, who are the triumphant Church, and the believers striving on earth, who are the militant Church; all are one house. The life of every believer becomes a spiritual house in which God dwells and works by His Holy Spirit to offer worship and good works.

A holy priesthood: every believer offers his body and his life as a sacrifice of love to God, through prayers, praise and works of goodness, and this is the general priesthood. Likewise the priests lead the Church in offering the Holy Sacraments before God, and this is the special priesthood.
Spiritual sacrifices: such as humility, repentance from sins, the rejection of selfishness, striving in worship, labor in service, and thanksgiving at all times.
By Jesus Christ: all the striving of life rests on the salvation that Christ the Redeemer gives us.

In the Old Testament God declared through the mouth of His prophets (Isa 28:16) that from the Jews would come Christ, the Savior of the world, whom He likens to a chief cornerstone, that is, the stone that joins two perpendicular walls. He is the foundation of the building, chosen by God for the redemption of mankind, and precious because He is the only-begotten Son, and whoever believes in Him is saved. When he lives his whole life in Him, he triumphs over the devil and is not put to shame in eternity, but enjoys the Kingdom.

Everyone who believes in Christ and lives by faith until the end of his life receives inexpressible honor and glory in heaven. As for those who refuse to believe in Christ, they will discover on the last day that He is the foundation of salvation, and eternal torment awaits all who rejected Him. Christ said this about Himself in (Lk 20:17).

A stone of stumbling and a rock of offence: Isaiah prophesied this about Christ (Isa 8:14). He is a shock to the sensual, since He deprives them of their evil pleasures, and an offence to the proud among the Jews, who hoped for Him to be an earthly king who would save them from the Romans, and likewise to the proud in the world, such as the Greeks, who wanted Him to be great on earth and not crucified and weak in outward appearance.
Being disobedient to the word: those who refuse faith do not obey the commandments of Christ.

Whereunto also they were appointed: in God's eternal knowledge He knows that they will refuse faith and receive eternal torment, even though these Jews ought to have been the people of God and the first to believe in Him. The Apostle makes clear that for unbelievers the Gospel of Christ will be against their lusts and earthly thoughts, so they do not obey it, and consequently it will condemn them on the last day and they will be cast into the eternal fire.
After speaking of those who reject faith, he speaks to the believers and gives them the following titles:

A chosen generation: the chosen people of God are those who believe in His word and in Christ the Savior. God promised the Jews of old that they would be His chosen people if they listened to His word, but if they refused they would not be His people (Ex 19:6). A royal priesthood: because its head is Christ, the King of kings.
An holy nation: believers become one holy Church in Christ.
A peculiar people: Christ purchased us with His blood so that we might live for Him.
That ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you: preaching Christ.
Believers in Christ become a holy people who live with Him in His Church and preach in His name in the whole world.

He addresses the Jews, who were not a people of God because of their sins, and likewise the Gentiles, who were far from God. But when they all believed, Jews and Gentiles, they became the Christian people of God. They had also been far from the mercy of God because of their persistence in sins, but by their faith and repentance they received God's mercy and His salvation through the Holy Sacraments, and endless mercies and blessings await them in heaven.
Here he speaks about the qualities of believers, which are:

1- Refusing lusts: considering that believers are strangers to the world, they feel that their homeland is heaven and that their life on earth is temporary. They are also sojourners, like one who stays a short time in a hotel or a guest in a house, but whose heart is attached to the place to which he will return, that is, the Kingdom. Therefore he asks them to keep away from evil lusts and all their sources, and not to mix with the wicked and with places of evil.
2- Honest conversation: he asks believers to behave well, with love and faithfulness in their dealings with others, however wicked those others may be.
Whereas they speak against you: you will be exposed to persecutions and false accusations from unbelievers, so bear them and continue your good treatment of them.
Glorify God in the day of visitation: when God visits unbelievers and they believe in Him, they will glorify Him because of your good conduct and your forbearance toward them.

He calls them to upright conduct toward those far from faith, however much they slander them with false accusations. This will help them, when those people believe, to glorify God because of the believers' forbearance toward them and their steadfastness in good conduct.

3- Submission to authorities: the Apostle declares that the authorities of the world are appointed with God's permission, and he calls them human ordinances. The king is the supreme head, and the governors or rulers are his assistants. He instructs us to submit to their orders and to all the laws of the state, for submission to them is for the sake of God, who permitted their presence in these positions, and God permitted their appointment to punish the wicked and to praise those who do good. The believer must therefore be a good citizen who respects all the laws of society.

4- Doing good: believers are children of God, the Maker of good things, so they must take care to do good at all times and to every person, and by their love they overcome evil, so that the ignorant who are far from faith find no opportunity to find fault in them.

5- True freedom: believers must also be free from sin, and this is true freedom, by their upright conduct, so that they keep away from the conduct of the wicked, who hide behind false freedom to justify their sins. True freedom does not conflict with God's commandments and is not at the expense of the comfort of others.
6- Love for all: we consider all people our brothers, so we love them and help them in all their needs.

7- The fear of God: since we feel the presence of the just God, who sees all our deeds and thoughts, we reject sin and submit to the orders of the state, which the king represents, so we respect him and honor him by obeying his orders.

The sum of your relationship with God and your love for Him appears in your love for those around you, your forgiveness when they wrong you, and even your striving to serve them. If you find a shortcoming in your service, examine yourself so that you repent of your sins, and review your relationship with God in order to develop it.
Servants: he means slaves and all hired workers.

Christianity confronted the problem of slaves not by stirring them up against their masters but by changing their hearts so that they love those for whom they work, and so live in peace with them, and sometimes the masters even set them free. Here he asks slaves and workers to submit with love to those for whom they work, not only to gentle masters but also to the harsh and hard-hearted, because violence is a sin that proclaims that its owner is weak and needs to be treated with love in order to remove the savage nature from him, "for love is strong as death" (Song 8:6), and whoever believes in it can live in peace and change those around him.

Offer your love and respect to everyone with humility, confident that humility and love are stronger than the pride and harshness of others, and be confident that your prayers will give you favor in their eyes, so that you win them or at least keep your peace and live with them in peace.

Whoever endures sufferings without having sinned, that is, when these sufferings are unjust to him, God compensates him with comforts within him and blessings in heaven, and counts his endurance a virtue for which God rewards him.

On the other hand, endurance of injustice is not counted a virtue if a person has sinned and met with bad treatment from others, for this is not injustice but a natural result of his faults. But whoever holds fast to doing good and is then wronged by others, this is great in the sight of God, who calls us to love our enemies and bless those who mistreat us (Mt 5:44-48).

He affirms that the Christian calling is to endure sufferings and to offer love instead of offence to the whole world, as Christ Himself did in His endurance of sufferings and His death for us, to be an example for us.
The Apostle affirms that Christ is an example for us in enduring sufferings while wronged, and he quotes from Isaiah (Isa 53:9) to make clear that He is without sin, but righteous and holy.

The love of Christ appears, while He endured the sufferings, in His not resisting evil with evil. He prayed for those who crucified Him and reviled Him, and was an example for us in committing our lives to God the just, who repays each one according to his works.

Christ bore the punishment of our sins on the cross to lift it from us, so that we may live in righteousness and reject the sin that caused all these sufferings to our Redeemer. Thus we receive redemption and healing from our sins because of Christ's endurance of sufferings for us, as Isaiah said (Isa 53:5).

Because of sin you were straying from the truth like lost sheep, but when you believed in Christ you became members of His Church, and He is the Shepherd of the Church, responsible for it, and its Bishop, that is, the One who watches over it with the eye of His care and orders all its needs.
Marital instructions
Obey not the word: they refuse the good news of Christ.
Without the word: by love and good treatment.

He asks wives to submit to the leadership of the man, for a woman by her nature inclines to be led by a man whom she trusts, and a man by his nature is suited to lead the woman and care for her. This submission must be in love, so that it wins the hearts of husbands even if they are pagans, as it was at the beginning of Christianity when a pagan wife believed and her husband had not yet believed. Her conduct in the submission of love wins her husband even if she has no opportunity to preach to him in plain words about Christ, for he notices a change in her conduct, namely her submission out of love, and discovers that the secret of this is her faith in Christ.

For the sake of the fear of God he asks women to be careful about their conduct and behavior, so that it is not out of fear of her husband or of anyone else but for the sake of God, because fear of people is temporary and is exposed, whereas the fear of God is lasting and gives peace and strength.
He forbids them excessive concern for their appearance, and chooses three things from it:
1- Excessive attention to the hair: in the past they used to braid their hair into dozens of plaits.
2- The abundance of jewelry with which they adorn themselves.

3- Luxurious or stumbling clothes, or excessive preoccupation with fashion and attention-grabbing clothing. What is meant is that a woman should be moderate in her adornment and should not let her heart be much occupied with it, because her first concern is God.

He directs the woman's attention to care for the inner purity of her heart from all evil and corrupt thoughts, and to being distinguished by inner calm, which also appears in gentle dealings with others; for inner purity and spiritual virtues are the most precious thing before God, who is not concerned with material appearances and outward adornment.
He calls the woman to imitate the holy women of the Old Testament, who were obedient to their husbands and concerned with virtues, and who relied on God and not on their beauty and adornment.

He gives an example of the holy women of the Old Testament, our mother Sarah, who respected our father Abraham and submitted to him and called him "lord" to show her respect for him. If women feel the motherhood of this saint toward them, as the Jewish men feel the fatherhood of Abraham, then wives should walk like Sarah in being concerned with doing good and relying on God and not on outward adornment. And as God gave Sarah surpassing beauty, He gives wives grace and beauty in the eyes of their husbands.
May you be confident that the purity of your heart, your love and your spiritual virtues are stronger than every outward appearance and give you grace in the eyes of God and in the eyes of people.
He asks husbands for three things:

1- Wisdom (discernment): in understanding the nature of the woman, which differs from the nature of the man, and taking that into account in dealing with her, such as her distinction in emotion, precision, attention to details, and so on.

2- Not being rough (the feminine vessel as the weaker): taking into account that the woman is weaker in physical strength, so the man does not use his physical strength to achieve his demands or threaten with words of violence and insults.

3- Being occupied with eternity (heirs together of the grace of life): the woman is like the man in her inheritance of the Kingdom, so the man takes into account that the span of life is temporary and is a means of preparation for eternity. He is therefore not preoccupied with fulfilling his material desires, nor does he become angry and furious if they are not fulfilled, because his anger or harshness will make his prayer unacceptable before God, and indeed will make him lose his peace, so that he cannot feel prayer and the comfort in it.

May you take into account the natures of others and love them in the way that suits them and not as you yourself see fit, and remember that you will be one with them in the Kingdom around Christ, so that you easily give up the passing matters of this world over which you differ.
He asks all the members of the family for the following:

1- Unity of mind: which is achieved through dialogue and understanding and each one's sensitivity to the other, so that they arrive at one feeling and one thought and come out with one opinion, and in this way they overcome all divisions and clashes.
2- Love: offering love by making excuses for those who err, having compassion on the weak, and dealing with gentleness and tenderness in everything.

3- Not resisting evil: no one flares up because of another's anger and returns insulting words or bad deeds; on the contrary, we quench evil with good deeds and words of love and blessing, which declare our good nature as children of God.

4- Good speech: he quotes the words of the Psalm (Ps 34:12-14) to show the importance of keeping away from bad words such as insults or deceit and lying, and rather the Christian expresses himself with good words that show the love that is within him.

5- Peace: if the devil stirs up any problems, they must be stopped, not only by refraining from evil words but also by showing love and doing good with others, so that their agitation calms. Thus the Christian seeks to make peace and sacrifices for it whatever the cost, so he pursues it in his way with all his energy, and God will help him by answering his requests and blessing his life. For whoever sacrifices and endures for the sake of peace is not wronged but is distinguished by God's blessings and fellowship, whereas whoever insists on evil defies God and deserves divine punishment.

7- Reassurance: God's promise to those who do good and make peace, for He grants them inner peace and protects them from evil and does not allow anything to harm them spiritually and hinder the salvation of their souls. Consequently they do not fear people however harsh they may be; on the contrary, God compensates them for their endurance of pain and offence with blessings in their life on earth and in the Kingdom.

8- Inner holiness: God directs the attention of His children to care for consecrating the heart to Him so that they enjoy fellowship with Him, and when they deal with others their faith and their hope in eternity will appear, and their words will be strong and gentle, showing the wicked their weakness and so drawing them to repentance.

9- Purity: care for purity of heart and the rightness of the inner intention, so that your good deeds are linked to a pure heart, and consequently the wicked are put to shame before God for their wickedness and their bad treatment of you, and your endurance of injustice becomes great in God's sight. For whoever suffers for his faults accepts the natural result of his own conduct, but whoever endures offences while his conscience is good and his deeds are good has the divine reward, because it is God who permitted these offences in order to reward His children with inexpressible blessings.

Be confident that your endurance of sufferings because of your seeking peace is the conduct of the children of God, and the blessings that await you for your endurance are very many; indeed you are greater than the one who offends you. So do not be shaken however much others cast doubt on you, but have compassion on the offender and pray for him.

If the children of God endure sufferings for the sake of doing good and making peace, they are in this following the example of Christ, who suffered, being righteous, for sinners, to save them from eternal death. Having died in the flesh on the cross, He rose on the third day to give life to all who believe in Him, and He makes the endurance of sufferings, with all the troubles that come upon the body and soul, a means for the life and growth of the spirit within everyone who endures. It is a call to bear with sinners and offenders as Christ bore, and He promised spiritual blessings on earth and then in eternal life. Thus sufferings bring us near to God when we endure them: Christ died once on the cross so that we might be put to death for His sake and endure sufferings every day, and so enjoy the life of the Spirit in us.
By which: God in Christ.
Prison: Hades.

When Christ died on the cross, His soul was separated from His body, but His divinity remained united to both. So Christ went with His divinity united to the human soul to Hades to preach to all the believers of the Old Testament that redemption had been accomplished, in order to bring them up with Him to Paradise.

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic and St. Cyril, the pillar of the faith, say in their interpretation of this verse that with the souls of the saints who were in Hades there were the souls of some people who lived in the days of the Flood and did not believe and enter the ark with Noah, but when the waters rose and they began to drown they repented and declared their faith. Though they were not saved from the Flood with Noah inside the ark, God took account of their faith and their repentance, which came at the end of their life, and when He descended to Hades He saved them with the rest of the believers and brought them up to Paradise. Thus the longsuffering of God appears, and His concern for the salvation of every person who believes, even at the last moment of his life, like the right-hand thief.

As God saved Noah and those with him in the ark from the Flood, He saves all of us from eternal death when we die to our sins by being immersed in the water of Baptism. Baptism is not a material washing of the body as human eyes see it, but a new birth and a purification of the heart from every sin, which we receive as a blessing from Christ's redemption of us on the cross.
Authorities and powers: ranks of angels.

After Christ rose from the dead, He ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of God, that is, He came into the glory and power that were His from eternity, which He had temporarily set aside before our eyes by appearing in the flesh and enduring sufferings to redeem us. And in His heavenly glory all the angels in their various ranks praise Him and serve Him.

God seeks your salvation however far away you are or fallen in sin. Trust in His love and rise quickly to make up for all that is past; He will forgive you everything, and your place in His heart is not shaken, for He has loved you from eternity and awaits your return to Him.
Sufferings in the life of the children of God

entries.section: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

paragraphs.text: This intention: enduring sufferings.

Christians face troubles not only in controlling their lusts but in enduring the mockery of the wicked who used to share their lusts with them. Therefore the Apostle Peter encourages them that Christ endured many sufferings for our redemption, so we follow His example, knowing that any sufferings we bear make us stop and grow weary of sin, for sufferings encourage us to repent.

entries.section: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

paragraphs.text: The Christian feels that life is limited, so repentance drives him to leave the lusts of the wicked and to be concerned with carrying out God's commandments and will.

entries.section: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter alerts us to the waste of our past life in various sins; what has happened is enough, so let us now try to use our life for living with God. He lists a group of evident sins in which believers formerly shared with the pagans, which are:
Lasciviousness: debauchery and excess in fornication.
Lusts: impurity, or the love of foods and possessions...
Excess of wine: that is, continuing in drunkenness.
Revellings: complaining and rebellion.
Banquetings: sitting with the wicked and taking part in their deeds.
Abominable idolatries: with all the accompanying evil lusts that they include.

entries.section: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

paragraphs.text: The wicked are surprised at the believers because they have repented of the lusts that they used to practice with them, and also of the rush and persistence in every form of debauchery, which drives these wicked people to abuse the believers and accuse them of sins they did not commit.

entries.section: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

paragraphs.text: The Apostle makes clear that the wicked Gentiles will be called to account for all their evil deeds on the Day of Judgment. He says this to establish the believers in repentance and in rejecting evil lusts.

entries.section: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

paragraphs.text: For this cause: for the sake of the great Day of Judgment, on which God will call man to account for all the evil he has done.
The dead: those who believed in Christ and then died.
Be judged according to men: the wicked judge them and persecute them to death.

That they might live according to God: life after death in the Paradise of bliss and then the Kingdom of Heaven. So that people would not be condemned on the Day of Judgment, the Apostles preached everywhere, and many believed and endured sufferings from the wicked until they were martyred, and this is the judgment of men that comes upon the flesh only. But these dead believers live in the Spirit with God in the Paradise of bliss.

Do not be distressed when some sufferings come upon you, but make them a reason to remember your sins and repent of them, knowing that our life on earth is short, so that you hasten to seize opportunities and draw near to God.

When we remember the end of our life and the Day of Judgment we become spiritually vigilant, and this is sobriety, so we pay attention and take care with our prayers, which bring us near to God and are also our whole life in heaven; that is, through prayers we prepare for our eternal life.
When we love God through many prayers, a feeling of love for others grows in us, so we are concerned to serve them, and if we see their sins we do not judge them but cover them.

Love of the brethren results in the care to show hospitality to strangers, and we do not do it as a heavy duty and so murmur about it, but with love and joy, because by this we receive Christ, as Abraham received strangers and discovered that he had received God and the angels (Gen 18).

If one of the believers is distinguished by a gift, such as preaching or the ability to provide for the needs of the needy, he is not proud, but feels that this gift is a grace from God and that he is a steward of it, to use it in the service of the Church.

Because gifts are from God, the preacher must speak the words of the Holy Bible and the mind of the Church and not his personal ideas. And whoever performs any service should rely on prayer to receive God's power from it, and servants should glorify God and thank Him before and after their service, because He is the One who acts in the service.

Your love for people reveals the measure of your love for God, for love is your only work in the world. Take care to cover people's sins, make excuses for them and help them with all your strength, because your abilities are a gift from God that increases in proportion to how much you use it in caring for others.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: The Apostle reassures the believers in the midst of the sufferings that meet them from those who persecute them. Even if the persecutions appear like a fiery trial that burns and destroys many aspects of their life, they should not be troubled, because this is to be expected from the evil world that persecutes the children of God.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: He gives them the good news that, as they have shared in enduring sufferings and persecutions for the sake of Christ, they will share in His eternal glories, and thinking about these glories gives them joy in the midst of their sufferings.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: He continues his encouragement of the persecuted believers: the insults to which they are exposed make them worthy to receive a greater grace from the Holy Spirit, who comforts them and makes them feel His presence with them and also promises them heavenly glories. Thus, even if the insults appear as blasphemy against Christ on the part of the wicked, they are counted as glory and a crown of blessing for the suffering believers, for Christ is glorified because of their endurance of these sufferings for His sake.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: He forbids believers to suffer because of their sins, because they must walk in righteousness and keep away from evident sins such as murder or theft or any evil deeds that society rejects and punishes, even small sins such as meddling in the private affairs of others, which troubles them and rouses them against us. The personal freedom of every person must be respected, because these are the sufferings to which the wicked are exposed because of their evils, and they are rejected by God and are not counted as being for the sake of God.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: But if the believer suffers because he is a Christian and walks in the commandments of God, these sufferings are counted as being for the sake of God, and He supports him in them and rewards him for them.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: The Apostle encourages us to hold to a life of righteousness and to reject sins by remembering the justice of God, who punishes the wicked, and His discipline will begin with His Jewish people by the destruction of the temple of God in Jerusalem, which Christ foretold to them (Mt 23:38). If God begins by disciplining His children the Jews for their unbelief in Christ, how great will be His discipline and punishment of the wicked pagans who refuse to believe in Him and persist in their sins.

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: He continues to remind them of the justice of God, which requires that righteous believers strive by the grace of their God until He saves them. And naturally the wicked and the ungodly will have no place in the Kingdom, but eternal torment awaits them. This shows the same meaning as is found in (Prov 11:31).

entries.section: (3) The reward of those who suffer

paragraphs.text: At the end of his encouragement of the believers who suffer because of their faith, he calls them to rely on God the Maker of good things, who does not forget their love and endurance and rewards them with heavenly glories.

When afflictions and sufferings befall you without your having sinned, accept them from God, confident of His appreciation of your endurance and looking to the eternal reward, and do not offend those who offend you but pray for them. Advice for priests and young people

The Apostle directs his recommendations to the shepherds, who are the bishops and priests, whom he gathers in the word "elders," which in Greek is "presbyteros," meaning bishops or priests, as it occurs in Greek in (Acts 20:17, 28). He speaks with humility and says "their fellow elder" and not their superior, to show his sympathy with them, for he suffers the sufferings of persecution as they do and awaits the glories of heaven with them. He is an eyewitness of the sufferings of Christ, His crucifixion and His resurrection, which he preaches.
Overseers: that is, supervisors, and he means the bishops, because the word bishop means overseer.
The Apostle Peter summarizes his recommendations as follows:

1- Shepherding the children of God: he directs their attention to the fact that their people are God's flock and they are stewards over it, so that they may be faithful before Him in their shepherding of His people.

2- Willingly: he asks them for vigilance, oversight and care for the people, not as a heavy duty to which they are compelled, but they strive with love, by their own choice, to care for every individual.
3- Free service: they should have no material greed behind the service, but with love and zeal they serve for the sake of God.

4- Not lording it over: they do not exploit their position as shepherds to domineer over the money of the Church and use it according to their own wishes, but with wisdom they listen to the opinions of those who help them and fulfill the wishes of their people.
5- Being an example: in all their words and actions, so that the servants and the people may follow their example.

He encourages them to be faithful in their service, for which they will receive their reward in eternity, when Christ appears, the Chief Shepherd and just Judge, and gives them the crowns of eternal heaven, unlike the glories of earth, which fade away.
Take care to serve everyone around you, especially if you have responsibility for others, knowing that your love and labor are very precious to God and He will reward you for them in heaven.
He advises the young with a group of commandments, which are:

1- Humility and submission: they submit and obey the priests and the elderly, and indeed they also submit to one another with humility, because God gives grace to the humble and, on the contrary, rejects and resists the proud.

He encourages the young to be humble, whether toward their elders or toward one another, for this is a proof of their humility before God, and a great reward awaits them, which is that God supports them in afflictions and comforts their hearts so that they rise above the affliction while they are in it, and then lifts them up on the last day to the heavenly glories and compensates them for all their endurance during their humility.
2- Relying on God: trust in God's love and power, so we place all our problems and needs before Him, and in His fatherhood He cares for us, supplies all our needs and solves our problems.

3- Spiritual vigilance: he calls them to constant spiritual attention and watchfulness, because the devil, our enemy, tries to seize any opportunity to make us fall into sin. He likens him to a lion for his ferocity, but he is unable to harm us; he goes around everywhere and tries to make us fall, but he cannot so long as we are spiritually vigilant and hold fast to God.

4- Spiritual striving: he calls us to resist the devil with all the exercises of spiritual striving, holding fast to our faith however our weakness appears or our sins multiply, especially since the devil fights all people in the world, but believers are distinguished by the grace of God that supports them. If our unbelieving brethren in the world try to reject sins, then all the more we believers, who rely on the power of God, resist him and triumph over him.

He encourages them to carry out the preceding commandments, reminding them of the heavenly glories that God has prepared for them because they endured and suffered for His sake in their spiritual striving, and he also promises them that He will:
1- Perfect every lack and weakness in them.
2- Establish them in the faith.
3- Strengthen them against the wars of the devil.
4- Enable them for every good work.
And then they glorify God, to whom belong power and dominion over all creatures forever.

Be confident that your love and labor for the sake of God have a great reward, and He also supports you in carrying out His commandments. So take courage, however great your weakness and however much the devil's wars increase, because God loves you and perfects you by His grace until you obtain His heavenly glories.

Silvanus: known by the name Silas (Acts 15:22), who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey (Acts 15:40) and wrote the First and Second Epistles to the Thessalonians (1 Thess 1:1, 2 Thess 1:1) and served with Timothy in Corinth (2 Cor 1:19). He was with Mark the Apostle in Egypt and wrote this epistle for the Apostle Peter because of his mastery of Greek, and Peter describes him as faithful because of his commitment and his bearing the responsibilities of the ministry.
As I suppose: this does not mean doubt, and in the Greek language it means certainty.

The Apostle Peter declares that he dictated his epistle to Silvanus because he is skilled in Greek, and he also sent it with his own hand, so that it includes these sermons and counsels that establish believers in the grace of God. The Apostle Peter condensed these sermons into these words, but he has much more that he wants to say.
Babylon: Babylon of the Stairs (Babylon el-Darag) in ancient Egypt, in Egypt.
The elect: the Church in Egypt, which St. Mark founded.

Peter wrote his epistle in Babylon in ancient Egypt, so he sends the greetings of the Church of Egypt to the churches of the world, and this Church is chosen by God together with the rest of the churches. He also sends the greetings of the founder of this Church, who is Mark the Apostle, and he describes him as his son because he is younger than he, and also his relative, since he is the husband of the daughter of the paternal uncle of the father of Mark the Apostle.
In conclusion he asks all believers to deal with one another in peace, and he also sends them his personal peace, filled with love and fatherhood.
Offer words of love and peace to everyone you meet, so that you absorb the agitation and tension in him, win him, and show Christ to him.
